text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike observed for continuous-batching path in us-west-2. Affected service: runtime-infer. Rolling degradation starting 2142000000. Auto-fallback to small-quant model triggered for ~12% of requests. Paging oncall: @alex :rotating_light:

alex: saw it, joining. any obvious recent deploys?

sam: no deploys in last 2 hours. saw queue depth jump on batch-scheduler metric. p95 ~420ms -> 1.6s, p99 ~2.4s -> 6.8s. streaming stalls increasing.

alex: checking traces. attached top traces show long wait in batch-queue for mixed seqlen bundles, and KV cache churn on host-12.

ryan: seems like large-chat requests (seq>2048) are getting bundled with short ones, causing batching expansion. scheduler fairness skewed after yesterday's config change to prefer latency for dedicated tier.

alex: ok mitigation plan: 1) temporarily restrict continuous-batching to max_batch_size=12 for streaming routes, 2) force-separate streams by seq-length class, 3) trigger KV eviction on hosts with high mem pressure, 4) add a short-term preempt policy to prefer streaming over batch background.

marta: +1. how to apply quickly?

alex: running patch now. infra-bot, can you push max_batch_size override to prod routing config for route /v1/stream and /v1/generate?

infra-bot: Deploy triggered: config-override/max_batch_streaming_usw2. CID: cfg-2142000000-ovr. Rolling to 3 AZs (a,b,c). ETA ~60s per AZ.

sam: also adding a quick KV eviction on host-12: ssh run -> sudo /opt/runtime/bin/kvctl evict --threshold 0.8. Doing now.

alex: running a quick smoke:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"short chat"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream | head -n1
```
Observed stream latency back to ~200ms median in canary. p99 trending down.

ryan: scheduler tweak deployed: fairness_weight_stream=1.4 -> 2.0 for 10m window to prefer streaming jobs.

alex: monitoring dashboards: batch-queue latency and schedule-wait dropping. KV memory on host-12 reduced from 92% -> 66% after eviction.

sam: logs show a noisy tenant had spikes of long-sequence requests at 2139k. We've rate-limited that tenant briefly to prevent churn.

marta: customer impact? any errors or user-facing retries?

alex: at peak we saw ~0.6% request timeouts for streaming endpoints and some 429s when fallback model capacity hit. No data loss. A couple customers with strict SLOs saw degraded p99; contacted support to open incident tickets for top 3 affected orgs.

marta: ok, prepping handoff. alex, can you summarize what to watch in next 30m?

alex: summary for oncall shift:
- primary cause: mixed-seqlen batching + scheduler fairness change led to oversized batches and long queue waits.
- mitigations applied: max_batch_size cap for streaming routes, seq-length routing split, KV eviction on hot hosts, temporary fairness_weight increase for streaming, brief tenant rate-limit.
- metrics to watch: runtime.batch_queue_time.p95/p99, streaming.latency.p95/p99, host.mem.kv_usage, fallback_rate, tenant-noise metric.
- rollback knobs: revert config-override, revert fairness weight, re-enable larger batches after traffic stabilizes.

marta: thanks. I'm taking handoff at 2142000600. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if p99 > 2s for more than 5m.

alex: handing to @marta. I'll stay nearby until stable. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: config-override completed in all AZs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Mitigations applied. Status: monitoring. Incident severity: sev3 -> under observation.

marta: creating incident summary ticket and notifying support to follow up with customers. tagging #customer-impact.

sam: one follow-up action: add a scheduler test for mixed-seqlen stress in staging and an alert for KV churn correlated with batch-size growth.

marta: added to backlog and assigned to queue-owner. closing active pager for now, will reopen if regress.

alex: thanks team.

marta: end of thread.
